headline: Two critical Wasmtime sandbox-escape flaws join PHP2Shell exploitation and the LiteLLM 1.107.0 compromise as the top stories

bullets.text: New: The Hacker News reports two critical Wasmtime flaws that could let malicious WebAssembly modules escape the sandbox. Separately, GitHub's advisory database lists a critical Cranelift miscompilation bug in Wasmtime (CVE-2026-115889).

PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) is now being successfully exploited in the wild. Fixes are in 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35; a third bug, CVE-2026-115560, will not get an emergency fix.
LiteLLM: a leaked master key let attackers steal GitHub tokens and hijack the release pipeline. Version 1.107.0 on PyPI and Docker stole credentials through Python startup hooks.

Fortinet has patched critical FortiOS flaws found with AI help; the brief names no CVEs or fixed versions. CISA's deadline passed today for exploited Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator (CVE-2026-114625) and Collabora Online CODE (CVE-2026-110447) flaws.

Still open: unpatched Tailscale SSH flaws could let a hacked tailnet device reach root on other servers, and a planted file in a Downloads folder tried to trick an AI coding agent into installing malware.

Breaches: Quest Diagnostics patient personal and health data, 11.7 million CAPCOM ID accounts, and over 70,000 firewall and VPN credentials exposed. SITCON eased to 4 (GUARDED); the last 7 days scored 1.25x the 90-day average.

actions: If you run untrusted WebAssembly in Wasmtime, check the Wasmtime security advisories and upgrade to the fixed release as soon as it is available.
Update PHP to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35, rebuild images that bundle PHP, and check exposed PHP hosts for compromise.
Search lockfiles, images and CI caches for litellm 1.107.0. If it ever ran, treat the host as compromised and rotate every credential it could read.
Update FortiOS to the fixed release for your branch, and patch or take offline Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator and Collabora Online (CODE server).
If you use Tailscale SSH, restrict ACLs so only trusted devices can SSH to servers, and watch for Tailscale's fix.
Require approval for installs and shell commands in AI coding agents, and keep them out of untrusted folders like Downloads.
